title: 1990 AHSME Problem 18
statement: First \(a\) is chosen at random from the set \(\{1,2,3,\ldots,99,100\},\) and then \(b\) is chosen at random from the same set. The probability that the integer \(3^a+7^b\) has units digit \(8\) is

solutions.text:
The units digits of \(3^a\) for \(a\equiv1,2,3,0\pmod4\) are \(3,9,7,1,\) while those of \(7^b\) are \(7,9,3,1.\) A sum ending in \(8\) occurs for the residue pairs \[ \begin{aligned} (a,b)\equiv{}&(2,2),(3,0),\\ &(0,1)\pmod4. \end{aligned} \] Each residue occurs \(25\) times among \(1,\ldots,100,\) so the probability is \(\frac{3}{16}.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: The units digits of both powers repeat with period \(4\)
List the residue pairs \((a\bmod4,b\bmod4)\) that produce a units digit of \(8\)
